pillarForecast.why: Open-the-exit is the form he picked himself; a visible gate from arena entry gives the dodge a destination, so expect explicit approval on the first run.
The door slam only crushes what he chose to drag along, which reads as his idea; B strengthens this by tying lured kills to the escape.
Decoy and pocket mine are gone and dash is always on the same key, so no control friction; new elements are in the world, not on the keyboard.
Bots average ~4 of 6 arenas in ~90s; with 3 hearts and the alarm spike, his runs from arena 1 may still end before 2 minutes, though checkpoints soften it.
Chargers enter at arena 4 alongside lasers and the 1.7x alarm spawns; that pile-up is where 'cheap' deaths returned before.
Continuous spawning removes the lone-enemy stall; the only dead-air risk is waiting on A's timer with nothing near a hazard.

biggestRisk: The exit-open alarm (1.7x spawns) stacked with chargers and lasers from arena 4 on could make the moment of escape feel like a chaotic scramble rather than a planned getaway, producing deaths he calls cheap right as the climax should land; secondarily, the A/B difference is so subtle (only the exit % climb rate) that he may not perceive it and the comparisons will mostly read 'same'.
abVerdict: Slight preference for B (~58%), expressed indirectly rather than as an explicit A/B call: B runs more likely tagged clever/satisfying and described in terms of 'killing them opens the door', while A runs more likely mention waiting on the exit or the alarm scramble. A sizeable chance (~35%) he doesn't notice any difference between variants.
